A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Revisiting Agnostic Boosting by the same authors. All pages, algorithms, equations and appendices support comparison; v2 retains the earlier proof framework and adds Appendix E.

before.justification: V1 reports theoretical algorithms, bounds and proofs, but no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis results.

after.justification: V2 remains theoretical, including its new lower-bound constructions. Its checklist also marks experimental results, settings and statistical reporting as not applicable.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the same confidence amplification, correlation-based AdaBoost, exhaustive relabeling, margin filtering and validation selection. The new lower-bound construction does not alter the proposed boosting procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or performs evaluations. Both study agnostic binary classification theoretically; Appendix E introduces mathematical hard instances.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates baseline methods experimentally. Changes to the analytical comparisons with prior boosting methods are covered under T1 and R1.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an empirical evaluation protocol. The three-way sample split, boosting iteration rule and margin grid in Algorithms 1 and 2 are unchanged.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity analyses or case studies. The added appendix contains theoretical lower-bound proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, error bars or significance tests. Confidence probabilities and concentration inequalities belong to the theoretical arguments.

E6.justification: Neither version reports measured scores, experimental rankings or empirical findings. The added and corrected mathematical bounds are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: V2 adds Theorem 1.2 and Appendix E, including a Hadamard-based hard-instance construction and agnostic-learning lower-bound derivations. Appendix A.2.2 adds a formal reduction between the Kalai–Kanade and Feldman weak-learning definitions, and Lemma D.1 extends v1 Lemma 23 to real-valued hypotheses. The new headline lower bound and its appendix statement have inconsistent dependence on the advantage parameters.

C1.justification: V1 conjectures optimality up to logarithmic factors and identifies proving lower bounds as future work. V2's abstract, introduction and conclusion claim a nearly matching lower bound that settles the sample complexity up to logarithmic factors.

C2.justification: V2 explains how its lower-bound construction produces the remaining logarithmic gap and expands the discussion of boosting's oracle access and computational relationship to ERM. The exponential-time limitation remains, while future work shifts toward computational efficiency and removing logarithmic factors.

D1.justification: The operational details in Algorithms 1 and 2 are retained. Neither version provides an implementation, hardware specifications, measured runtime or code/data access instructions; the added checklist supplies no such resources.

R1.justification: V2 adds Alon et al. (2023) as inspiration for the lower-bound construction and Bartlett–Ben-David (1999) and Ben-David et al. (2000) for ERM hardness. It also extends the Feldman/Kalai–Kanade comparison in Appendix A, while retaining the existing boosting literature coverage.

P1.justification: The introduction is reorganized around lower and upper bounds, related-work passages and Appendix A receive substantial rewriting, and Appendix A gains a clearer subsection hierarchy. V2 also introduces section-based statement numbering, funding acknowledgments and a conference checklist.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a different document template throughout, changing typography, spacing, the title and author block, running headers and equation layout. Both algorithm displays are reformatted, including moving their captions below the pseudocode. No empirical figures or result tables are added.

improvement.justification: Appendix E adds substantial lower-bound analysis addressing v1's central conjecture, and Appendix A clarifies relationships between weak-learning definitions. However, Theorem 1.2 uses (γ−ε₀)² in its denominator, whereas Theorem E.1 and its construction use γ², without reconciling these dependencies for general ε₀. This mismatch affects the new claim of settling sample complexity. The valuable additions and unresolved scope of the central claim prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
